newsitem.title: USA: Campbell to sell German chilled food unit.
newsitem.headline: Campbell to sell German chilled food unit.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. said Wednesday it will sell its Beeck-Feinkost GmbH chilled foods businesss in Germany to Gilde Buy-Out Fund, a Dutch venture capital firm.
Financial terms were not disclosed, but Campbell said Beeck managers will participate in the purchase.
Campbell, which bought the privately held gourmet salad and deli products business in 1987, said the unit had sales of about $65 million last year.

The sale -- part of Campbell's previously announced plan to divest non-strategic businesses -- includes the Beeck brand name and two manufacturing facilities in Hamburg and Cuxhaven, Germany, with about 360 employees.
Gilde Buy-Out Fund is managed by Gilde Investment Management, a global venture capital investor based in Utrecht, the Netherlands.
The sale is expected to close by June, the company said.
Campbell, based in Camden, N.J., announced earlier this month the sale of its Marie's salad dressing and dip business to Dean Foods.
Campbell's stock fell 25 cents to $46.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
